<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{th:main}
There exists a simple cubic graph $G$ on $20$ vertices such that $\chi''(G)=4$ and $\chi''_\ell(G)=5$.
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:sameColour}
In every total colouring of $K_{2,3}$ with $4$ colours, the two vertices in the part of the bipartition of cardinality $2$ receive the same colour.
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Consider a total colouring with $4$ colours, say red, blue, green and yellow. Let the vertices of $K_{2,3}$ be $a,b,v_1,v_2,v_3$ where $\{a,b\}$ is the part of the bipartition of size $2$. 

Suppose, to the contrary, that $a$ is red and $b$ is blue. Then each of the vertices $v_1,v_2,v_3$ must be green or yellow. By the pigeonhole principle, we can assume that $v_1$ and $v_2$ are both green. Since $a$ is incident to three edges, each of the colours blue, green and yellow must appear on one such edge. However, since $v_1$ and $v_2$ are green, the only edge incident to $a$ that can be green is $av_3$. Similarly, the only edge incident to $b$ that can be green is $bv_3$. However, the vertex $v_3$ is now incident to two green edges, which is a contradiction.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
